Back to Sirrak

Last updated: 25 November 2026 · Applies to 1.1.0

Security policy

  • Report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub Security Advisories — never in a public issue.
  • Sirrak has no server and no telemetry endpoint to attack; release builds are minified and store data in app-private storage.
  • Expected acknowledgement within 7 days; no paid bug bounty.

Supported versions

Sirrak is pre-1.0. Security fixes land on the newest release only; older builds are not patched.

Reporting a vulnerability

Please do not open a public issue for a security problem. Use the private advisory form at github.com/ahmadmhmdsy/sirrak/security/advisories/new and include:

  • the app version (Settings → About) and Android version,
  • the device or emulator model,
  • what you did, what you expected, and what happened,
  • a proof of concept if you have one.

You can expect an acknowledgement within 7 days and a status update within 30 days. We do not run a paid bug bounty.

Scope

In scope: the app itself (chat, the Library's models/downloads/media shelves and RAG, dictation, model download/import, Hugging Face browsing and the capped header probe, privacy surfaces) and the way it stores data on the device.

  • Out of scope: vulnerabilities in Android itself, in third-party model weights, and in the upstream llama.cpp / sherpa-onnx / LiteRT-LM code — report those upstream.
  • Out of scope: attacks that require a rooted device or physical access with an unlocked bootloader.

Design commitments relevant to security

  • No server-side component and no telemetry endpoint to attack.
  • Chats, documents, embeddings, models, network log and reports are stored in app-private storage.
  • The network audit is the single place that records outbound calls; it is bounded and local.
  • Release builds are minified with R8 and ship no debug-only cleartext permission (cleartext HTTP is debug-only, used by loopback device tests).
  • Model downloads are verified against the catalogue SHA-256 before installation.
  • The Hugging Face header probe is capped at 12 MB, accepts only ranged reads, and drops an authorization token when a redirect leaves huggingface.co.
  • A Hugging Face token is kept in memory only and never written to disk, the network log or a report.

Disclosure

We will credit reporters who ask to be credited, and publish a short advisory once a fix is available. Please give us a reasonable window before public disclosure.
